Everything a Yard or Riding Brand Needs

Competition Show Shirts

Long and short-sleeve show shirts with a stand collar, mesh side and underarm panels and a wicking finish. Club crest at the chest, rider name at the collar or cuff.

Riding Tights & Breeches

Full-seat and knee-patch styles in four-way stretch, with silicone grip, a high contoured waist, phone pockets and elastic or sock-style bottoms.

Technical Base Layers

Close-fit long and short-sleeve base layers with flatlock seams, thumb loops and mesh venting - the layer riders live in from autumn through spring.

Club Softshells & Jackets

Bonded softshells, lightweight showerproof jackets and padded gilets, cut for riding with a longer back and articulated sleeves. Embroidered club crests.

Yard Polos & Team Hoodies

The everyday yard kit: piqué polos, hoodies and quarter-zips for staff, grooms, liveries and supporters, in the same colours as the competition range.

Crests, Names & Numbers

Embroidery, 3D puff, sublimation and heat-transfer applied in-house. Club crest, sponsor logos, rider names and horse names on the same order.

Why Clubs and Equestrian Brands Order Factory-Direct

Riding kit is bought in small numbers and worn hard. A club needs twenty show shirts in its own colours, not two hundred; a new brand needs one breech style proved on real riders before it commits to a size run. Most suppliers answer both with a catalogue garment and a printed logo, because their minimums leave no room for anything else.

Ordering direct from the factory changes what is negotiable: the fabric weight, the grip layout, the length of the back hem, where the crest sits. Start with a trial order, or look at the wider sportswear range if you also kit out other teams.

Questions

What is the minimum order for custom equestrian apparel?

Twenty pieces per style. A riding club ordering show shirts for its members, or a new equestrian brand testing one breech style, both clear that comfortably - you do not need to commit to a full container to start.

Can you make full-seat and knee-patch breeches?

Yes, both. Silicone grip is applied as a printed pattern in the seat or at the knee, in a colour that matches or contrasts with the fabric. Tell us which discipline the breeches are for and we will suggest the grip layout riders in it expect.

Can you put our club crest and riders’ names on?

Yes. Crests are usually embroidered, and names, horse names and sponsor logos can be embroidered, sublimated or heat-applied on the same order. Send the crest in any format you have and we will redraw it for stitching at no charge.

What fabrics do you use for show shirts?

A wicking poly piqué at 150-180 GSM with mesh side and underarm panels. If you want a heavier or a softer handle, or a specific stretch, say so on the enquiry - the fabric is chosen per order rather than fixed.

Can you match our club or brand colours?

Yes. Send a Pantone reference and we match to it. Without one we will match to a physical sample or a printed swatch you post to us, and confirm with a lab dip before bulk production starts.

How long does production take?

Two to four weeks depending on the garment, after the sample is approved. Breeches and softshells sit at the longer end because of the grip application and the bonded fabric. Shipping is on top and depends on the method you choose.

Can we order a sample before committing?

Yes, and we recommend it for breeches in particular, where fit is the whole product. See trial orders for how that works.

Do you ship to the UK, EU and United States?

Yes, DDP - duty and tax are included in the quote so the price you approve is the price you pay. See the UK, Germany and EU and USA pages for the duty position in each.
